title: Consolidate GPU driver profiles and run compatibility probes for load-testing harness
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: The load-testing harness produces noisy performance signals across CI because GPU driver versions, CUDA toolkits, and runner images are not consistently pinned. Different runners (runner-v1 vs runner-v2) and host kernels produce p95 token latency variance and tokens/sec fluctuations that break regression detectors. Goal: Create a concise set of 'driver profiles' (driver + CUDA + image SHA + runner flag) that are supported by the harness, implement compatibility probe jobs in CI to verify profiles, and wire profile-aware baselines into the regression detection pipeline so alerts surface only for true regressions.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical driver profile manifest exists (CSV + pinned image SHAs) covering at least 3 representative hardware classes (A100, H100, T4) and 3 software stacks (CUDA 11.8, 12.1, 12.2).
CI probe jobs run weekly and on driver-image updates; probe job status is visible in the Bench Dashboard and gates regression alerts.
Benchmark harness updates annotate all load test results with 'driver_profile' metadata, and the regression detector groups comparisons by profile before computing p95 deltas.
Migration docs and a rollback plan are in Confluence; at least two downstream consumers (dedicated-quota tests and production smoke tests) adopt the manifest.
A follow-up PR adds automatic pinned-image updates (manual review step) with attached performance delta reports.
technical_notes: Driver profiles will be defined as tuples: <nvidia-driver-version, cuda-version, image:sha256, runner-tag> and stored in /manifests/bench-driver-profiles.csv in the infra repo.
Initial target driver versions: NVIDIA 535.86, 545.65; CUDA versions: 12.2, 12.1, 11.8. These are selected to cover common distro kernels and libcu versions we see in telemetry.
Pinned images will include both userland libs and the benchmark runner binary. Example image: ghcr.io/redwood/runtime-bench-runner:v2@sha256:4b7f...

Add a lightweight CI probe that runs a 30s steady-state tokens/sec test and p95 latency check; persist metrics to Bench Metrics (Prometheus + Grafana) and to the regression detector (time-series snapshots in S3).

Regressions are computed per-profile: compute rolling-median tokens/sec and p95 for the last 7 runs for the same profile; alert when current run deviates by >12% tokens/sec or p95 regresses >18% with p<0.01 bootstrap test.

Runner changes: stabilize runner-v2 as the canonical runner for new profiles. runner-v1 remains supported for legacy profiles but marked 'deprecated' in manifest. Add a runtime flag --profile-id to the runner to annotate telemetry.
Include a short probe that runs both MIG and non-MIG configurations for H100 to catch partitioning regressions affecting KV cache behavior.
Plan to add Honeycomb traces linking benchmark runs to underlying infra host IDs for debugging outliers; initial integration uses a synthetic span per run.
Performance noise mitigation: enable fixed clock stepping for synthetic token generation, warmup tokens fixed to 128, and deterministic seed for decoding sampling where applicable.
migration_plan: Publish draft manifest and solicits feedback from Runtime and Observability teams (3 business days review).
Merge manifest to infra repo and enable weekly CI probe job for new profiles in a feature branch (no gating).
Run 2 weeks of parallel traffic: results annotated by profile but not used for alerts; analyze deltas and update thresholds.
Flip gating: enable profile-aware grouping in regression detector and only surface alerts if CI probe history supports the new grouping.
Deprecate old unpinned profiles after 6 weeks with an automated notification to stakeholders.
Post-migration: Add periodic (monthly) reconciliation job that validates images by re-running the probe and comparing tokens/sec to stored baseline.
